claim_text: On the web, users typically read only about 20-28% of the words on a page during an average visit; reading share falls as word count rises.
source_title: Nielsen Norman Group -- How Little Do Users Read?
verify_method: Open the NN/G article and read the reported 20-28% range.
still_valid_note: Figure is an estimate that varies by page and intent; directionally robust.

claim_text: The F-shaped scanning pattern is ONE of several gaze patterns, not a design goal; it is a sign of skimming that good layout (front-loading, headings, bullets) can prevent or reshape.
source_title: Nielsen Norman Group -- F-Shaped Pattern of Reading (2017 update)
verify_method: Read the 2017 NN/G eye-tracking update.
contested_note: Often mis-cited as a universal law; NN/G stress it is one of several patterns and is preventable with good design.

claim_text: Front-loading conclusions and key information first (inverted pyramid) suits web skimming better than building up to a conclusion.
source_title: Nielsen Norman Group -- Inverted Pyramid writing for the web
verify_method: Read NN/G inverted-pyramid guidance.

claim_text: Working memory is sharply limited (classically about 7 plus or minus 2 items, with later estimates near 4 chunks), so interfaces should chunk information rather than present long undifferentiated lists.
source_title: Miller, The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two (Psychological Review)
verify_method: Read Miller (1956) and later working-memory reviews (e.g., Cowan 2001).
contested_note: The exact capacity is debated; modern estimates often cite ~4 chunks. Use as a chunking heuristic, not a hard limit.

claim_text: Cialdini identifies seven principles of influence -- reciprocity, commitment/consistency, social proof, authority, liking, scarcity, and unity (unity added in Pre-Suasion, 2016).
source_title: Cialdini, Influence (1984) and Pre-Suasion (2016)
verify_method: See Influence (6 principles) and Pre-Suasion (adds Unity).
still_valid_note: Original six principles plus Unity (2016); widely replicated across decades of research.

claim_text: Persuasion crosses into a deceptive 'dark pattern' when it manipulates choice against the user's interest (forced continuity, confirm-shaming, hidden costs); ethical influence makes the genuinely better choice easier, not the worse choice harder to avoid.
source_title: Nielsen Norman Group / Brignull -- Deceptive (dark) patterns
verify_method: Read NN/G deceptive-patterns taxonomy.

claim_text: Fogg's behaviour model holds that a behaviour occurs only when motivation, ability, and a prompt converge at the same moment (B=MAP); if behaviour fails, raise ability (reduce friction) or improve the prompt before adding motivation.
source_title: Fogg, A Behavior Model for Persuasive Design / Tiny Habits
verify_method: Read Fogg's Behavior Model paper.

claim_text: Conversion pages perform best with a single primary call to action; competing CTAs split attention and dilute the primary conversion goal.
source_title: CXL and GoodUI practitioner consensus on primary CTA
verify_method: Triangulate CXL + GoodUI + Unbounce guidance; graded as expert consensus, not RCT.

claim_text: Checkout/cart abandonment among purchase-intending users averages roughly 70%, and a meaningful share of abandonment is driven by trust, unexpected cost, and account-creation friction.
source_title: Baymard Institute -- Cart Abandonment Rate
verify_method: Open Baymard's cart-abandonment statistics page.
still_valid_note: Baymard is a practitioner Tier-1 usability lab (large-sample, not RCT); ~70% is an average across studies.

claim_text: Specific, benefit-led copy that names a concrete outcome converts better than vague feature lists; concreteness aids comprehension and recall.
source_title: Conversion copywriting practitioner consensus (CXL / Copyhackers)
verify_method: Triangulate CXL and Copyhackers; expert consensus, MODERATE.

claim_text: Organising content as a pillar page plus a cluster of supporting posts that interlink builds topical authority and helps both search ranking and internal navigation.
source_title: Topic-cluster model (HubSpot research; corroborated by SEO practitioners)
verify_method: Triangulate topic-cluster guidance across HubSpot + named SEO experts.

claim_text: Berger's STEPPS framework (Social currency, Triggers, Emotion, Public, Practical value, Stories) predicts sharing; high-arousal emotions (awe, anger, anxiety) increase sharing while low-arousal sadness decreases it -- arousal, not positivity, drives transmission.
source_title: Berger & Milkman, What Makes Online Content Viral? (JMR); Berger, Contagious
verify_method: Read Berger & Milkman (2012) JMR and Contagious (2013).

claim_text: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics (visibility of system status, match to the real world, user control, consistency, error prevention, recognition over recall, flexibility, minimalist design, error recovery, help) remain the baseline expert checklist for interface evaluation.
source_title: Nielsen Norman Group -- 10 Usability Heuristics
verify_method: Read the NN/G 10 heuristics article.

claim_text: Google's Core Web Vitals 'good' thresholds are LCP at or under 2.5 seconds, INP at or under 200 milliseconds, and CLS at or under 0.1; INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024.
source_title: web.dev -- Web Vitals (Core Web Vitals)
verify_method: Open web.dev/articles/vitals and confirm the three thresholds.

claim_text: Hick's Law (decision time rises with the number and complexity of choices) and Fitts's Law (target acquisition time depends on distance and size) justify reducing options and making primary targets large and close.
source_title: Laws of UX (Yablonski), citing Hick 1952 and Fitts 1954
verify_method: See Laws of UX and the original Hick (1952) / Fitts (1954) papers.

claim_text: E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trust) is a quality framework used in Google's Search Quality Rater Guidelines, NOT a direct ranking factor; Trust is described as the most important component.
source_title: Google Search Central -- Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
verify_method: Read Google's helpful-content guidance and the Search Quality Rater Guidelines.
contested_note: Widely mis-stated as a direct ranking signal; Google states raters do not directly affect ranking and E-E-A-T is a concept, not a metric.

claim_text: The Helpful Content System was folded into Google's core ranking in the March 2024 core update and is no longer a separate standalone signal.
source_title: Google Search Central -- March 2024 core update guidance
verify_method: Read Google's March 2024 core update announcement.

claim_text: Search intent splits into informational, commercial-investigation, transactional, and navigational; each query should be mapped to the page type that satisfies it (informational post, comparison, money/service page, or brand page).
source_title: Search-intent taxonomy (Google guidance; named SEO experts Aleyda Solis / Lily Ray)
verify_method: Triangulate Google intent guidance with Aleyda Solis and Lily Ray.

claim_text: For a service/lead-gen business, local SEO signals -- a complete Google Business Profile, consistent NAP, genuine reviews, and LocalBusiness/Service structured data -- materially affect visibility for location-qualified queries.
source_title: Google -- Local SEO / structured data guidance; practitioner corroboration
verify_method: Read Google's LocalBusiness structured-data docs.

claim_text: Generative Engine Optimization (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024) defines methods to raise a source's visibility in generative-engine answers; Cite Sources, Quotation Addition, and Statistics Addition were among the strongest, especially combined, with up to ~40% visibility uplift on GEO-bench.
source_title: Aggarwal et al., GEO: Generative Engine Optimization (KDD 2024, arXiv:2311.09735)
verify_method: Confirmed in the GEO full text (arXiv:2311.09735): 'GEO can boost visibility by up to 40% in GE responses. ... the efficacy of these strategies varies across domains.'
contested_note: The 'up to 40%' is a CEILING and is domain-dependent ('the efficacy of these strategies varies across domains') -- NOT a guaranteed uplift. Figure confirmed verbatim in the full paper (Numini fetched the full text, 9 Jun 2026): 'GEO can boost visibility by up to 40% in GE responses.'

claim_text: Numini measurement (Jun 2026, SerpApi AI Overviews, gl=us): for the head query 'pet relocation dubai to uk' the AI Overview cited 14 sources, 8 of which were in the top-10 organic results -- generative engines draw heavily from but also beyond the classic top 10.
source_title: Numini Research Elevator -- SERP/AI-Overview harvest (own measurement)
verify_method: Re-run harvest_serp.py --pillar lead_generation_content_system and inspect the overlap report.
still_valid_note: AI Overviews are volatile; re-measure regularly. This is a point-in-time snapshot.

claim_text: Clear entity definition and consistent facts across a site and the wider web improve a brand's chances of being retrieved and cited by generative engines (AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini).
source_title: GEO/AI-search practitioner consensus (Aleyda Solis; iPullRank/Mike King)
verify_method: Triangulate iPullRank and Aleyda Solis GEO/AI-search analyses.

claim_text: For AI writing, RAG supplies updatable, citable knowledge, prompt engineering controls behaviour/flexibility, and fine-tuning durably encodes brand voice at scale; the strongest default is RAG plus structured prompting, with fine-tuning optional.
source_title: RAG vs fine-tuning decision literature (Lewis et al. RAG, 2020; vendor guidance)
verify_method: Read Lewis et al. (2020) RAG paper plus current provider guidance.

claim_text: LLM writing systems hallucinate plausible but false facts; the mitigation is to ground output in a verified source (RAG), require citations, and refuse to assert anything not in the knowledge base.
source_title: Factuality/hallucination survey literature; RAG grounding evidence
verify_method: Read recent hallucination-survey papers; this mirrors the validation_gate design.

claim_text: Professional editing proceeds in order from structural (developmental) edit to line edit to copy edit; editing for the web also means plain-language and readability work, not just grammar.
source_title: Editorial standards (Chicago Manual of Style; plain-language guidance)
verify_method: See CMOS editing levels and plainlanguage.gov guidelines.

claim_text: Readability formulas (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) are heuristics, not ground truth; recent work shows formulas and even LLMs are weak predictors of true reading ease, so they should guide, not be gamed.
source_title: Readability prediction evaluation (arXiv:2502.11150); Flesch lineage
verify_method: Read arXiv:2502.11150 on readability-formula limitations.
contested_note: Treat readability scores as a guide, never a target to optimise blindly.

claim_text: A blog is a different machine depending on its job: an ad/affiliate blog optimises for pageviews/RPM, whereas a lead-generation/service blog optimises for qualified enquiries and cost-per-lead -- the success metric, architecture, and CTA all change with the objective.
source_title: Content-strategy canon (CMI/HubSpot) reconciled with the lead-gen objective
verify_method: Compare CMI/HubSpot strategy guides against a lead-gen funnel definition.
still_valid_note: Most published blog advice optimises for traffic; that is NOT this deployment's objective.

claim_text: Lead-gen content maps to funnel stages: TOFU informational ('do I need to relocate my pet?'), MOFU commercial-investigation ('best pet relocation Dubai to UK', costs, comparisons), and BOFU transactional ('pet relocation quote/book'); each post is tagged to a stage and to the money page it feeds.
source_title: TOFU/MOFU/BOFU funnel + search-intent model (practitioner consensus)
verify_method: Map sample queries to stages and to the route/service money page they feed.

claim_text: Route/service pages are the conversion assets ('money pages'); blog posts are demand capture that should internally link into the money pages (topical-cluster model). An informational post must never be a dead end.
source_title: Topical-cluster + internal-linking practitioner consensus
verify_method: Audit posts for at least one contextual link to a money page.

claim_text: Lead-capture forms convert better with fewer fields, reduced friction, and trust signals placed near the form; every non-essential field is a drop-off risk.
source_title: Baymard Institute -- form usability research
verify_method: Read Baymard's form-usability findings.

claim_text: Repeatedly checking an A/B test and stopping when it looks significant ('peeking') inflates false-positive rates; either fix the sample size in advance or use sequential testing with Type-I/FDR control.
source_title: Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020); Larsen et al., The American Statistician 78(2) 2024
verify_method: Read Kohavi/Tang/Xu (2020) and Larsen et al. (2024) on sequential testing.
